# Exact projective two-jet descent, including all facet contacts

This note gives an exact necessary condition at a projective-orbit depth
minimum of positive polytopal fibers. It removes the C2 cap-profile
assumption from the *descent test*, not from the quadratic certificate
in the previous note. It makes no claim that a failing numerical OC
bound forces such a descent. the contributor-derived; independent audit pending.

## 1. Parallel-cap profiles of a polytope

Let K be a full-dimensional compact d-polytope, d>=1, and fix a unit
vector u. Write

    F(t)=|K intersect {u.x>=t}|.

Then F is continuous and is a polynomial of degree at most d on each
open interval between consecutive values u.v at the vertices v of K.
It is constant outside the range of those values. In particular, finite
one-sided derivatives F'_-(T), F'_+(T), F''_-(T), F''_+(T) exist at
every T. For d=1, second derivatives on each side are zero.

Here are the details. For d=1 the assertion is the formula for the
length of an interval clipped by a moving endpoint. For d>=2, on an
interval containing no vertex height, the face incidence structure of
K intersect {u.x=t} is fixed. Whether the hyperplane crosses a given
face is decided by the minimum and maximum vertex heights of that
face. The vertices of the section are its intersections with a fixed
list of edges of K. Each intersection is affine in t. A pulling
triangulation with one fixed order on those section vertices therefore
has a fixed list of simplices throughout the interval. In orthonormal
coordinates on u-perp, each simplex has vertices affine in t, so its
(d-1)-volume is the absolute value of a determinant polynomial of
degree at most d-1, divided by (d-1)!. Its orientation cannot change
on this interval, because the pulling triangulation consists of
nondegenerate simplices there. Summing gives a polynomial section area.
Fubini, with |u|=1, integrates that polynomial to the asserted cap
polynomial of degree at most d. Bounded section areas and the slab
volume estimate prove continuity at each break. The finitely many
adjacent polynomials give finite one-sided derivatives of both orders.

This proof concerns volume only. A facet on the cap boundary has zero
d-volume but can have positive one-sided *first derivative*. That term
is retained below.

At a fixed threshold T abbreviate

    f^- = F'_-(T), f^+ = F'_+(T),
    h^- = F''_-(T), h^+ = F''_+(T).

Define the continuous positively homogeneous first derivative

    D(q)=f^+ q if q>=0, and f^- q if q<=0.            (1)

Both expressions give zero at q=0. Define the second coefficient

    E(q,r)=h^+ q^2+f^+ r                 if q>0,
           h^- q^2+f^- r                 if q<0,
           D(r)                         if q=0.     (2)

For t decreasing to zero through positive values, the exact expansion is

    F(T+t q+(t^2/2)r)
      =F(T)+t D(q)+(t^2/2)E(q,r)+o(t^2).             (3)

For q!=0 its sign selects one adjacent polynomial for all small t.
For q=0, the sign of r selects that polynomial and the displacement
is already of second order. If q=r=0 there is no displacement.
These observations prove (3), including every knot and endpoint.

For example, at an inside supporting facet of area S, with the cap
containing the body, f^-=0 and f^+=-S, hence D(q)=-S max(q,0).
At an outside supporting facet of area S, f^-=-S and f^+=0, hence
D(q)=S max(-q,0). At a proper cut, F' is continuous and equals minus
the section area, but F'' can still have different one-sided values.
Lower-dimensional supporting faces have f^-=f^+=0 and are also
included. No closed cap has been replaced by an open cap.

## 2. Finite critical covers on a fixed positive polytopal family

Let P be finite and K_p positive actual polytopal fibers. Let mu be
their sum of d-volume measures, M its mass, and beta their maximum
normalized ambient depth. Assume local minimality under positive affine
projective denominators on the base. All computations below use the
original fibers with density L(p)^(-d). Their projective images are
actual convex fibers at the image bases; halfspaces and candidates
correspond exactly, as proved in the projective-transform source.

Select finitely many critical circuits covering every deepest base.
Their groups have anchor points (p_i,x_i), and their caps and weights are

    H_ij={a_ij.p+u_ij.x>=b_ij}, |u_ij|=1,
    b_ij=a_ij.p_i+u_ij.x_i,
    mu(H_ij)=beta M,
    rho_ij>0, sum_j rho_ij=1, sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0.

At every nondeepest base retain one strictly cheaper finite circuit
cover of its whole fiber plane. The compact critical-cover theorem
in the archived source supplies these covers. They continue to be
strictly cheaper under sufficiently small changes of the finite
fiber weights.

Let F_ijp be the parallel-cap profile for K_p and u_ij at the initial
threshold T_ijp=b_ij-a_ij.p. Apply (1)-(2) to each such profile to
obtain D_ijp and E_ijp. Put V_p=|K_p| and F_ijp^0=F_ijp(T_ijp).

## 3. Actual affine-denominator and cap paths

Choose affine scalar functions A,B on the base and set

    L_t(p)=1+t A(p)+(t^2/2)B(p).                      (4)

For every fixed choice this is positive at all the finitely many bases
for small |t|, and hence positive on their convex hull. For each cap
choose base-normal vectors c_ij,e_ij and scalars s_ij,r_ij. Set

    a_ij(t)=a_ij+t c_ij+(t^2/2)e_ij,
    b_ij(t)=b_ij+t(c_ij.p_i+s_ij)
                      +(t^2/2)(e_ij.p_i+r_ij).      (5)

The continuous normals are unchanged and nonzero. In fiber p the
threshold becomes exactly

    T_ijp+t q_ijp+(t^2/2)r_ijp,
    q_ijp=s_ij-c_ij.(p-p_i),
    r_ijp=r_ij-e_ij.(p-p_i).                        (6)

The same letter r with three indices denotes the fiber threshold
acceleration, and with two indices denotes its value at the anchor.

The moved caps in group i cover the *entire* p_i plane for all small
positive t provided

    sum_j rho_ij s_ij<=0,
    and, when that sum is zero, sum_j rho_ij r_ij<=0. (7)

Indeed at that plane the weighted sum of their margins is

    -t sum_j rho_ij s_ij-(t^2/2)sum_j rho_ij r_ij,

because both the continuous normals and their initial margins balance.
Under (7) this is nonnegative. If every margin at a point were negative,
their positive weighted sum would be negative, a contradiction. Equality
in (7) is allowed; the caps are closed. The correspondence under the
projective map transfers this whole-plane cover to the image base.

## 4. Exact first and second raw budget coefficients

The total weighted mass has expansion M(t)=M+t M_1+(t^2/2)M_2+o(t^2),
where

    M_1=-d sum_p A(p)V_p,
    M_2=sum_p [d(d+1)A(p)^2-d B(p)]V_p.              (8)

The moving cap ij has expansion

    Q_ij(t)=beta M+t C_ij,1+(t^2/2)C_ij,2+o(t^2),

with

    C_ij,1=sum_p [D_ijp(q_ijp)-d A(p)F_ijp^0],       (9)

    C_ij,2=sum_p [E_ijp(q_ijp,r_ijp)
                   -2d A(p)D_ijp(q_ijp)
                   +[d(d+1)A(p)^2-d B(p)]F_ijp^0]. (10)

This follows by multiplying (3) by

    L_t(p)^(-d)=1-d t A(p)
           +(t^2/2)[d(d+1)A(p)^2-d B(p)]+o(t^2)

and summing a finite number of fibers. Thus the raw cap-budget
difference Q_ij(t)-beta M(t) has coefficients

    b_ij,1=C_ij,1-beta M_1,
    b_ij,2=C_ij,2-beta M_2.                          (11)

Every quantity uses the original mixed fiber-volume measure. There is
no substitution of ambient volume or replacement of a fiber sum by an
integral over the base.

## 5. Descent theorem and the minimum's necessary condition

**Descent theorem.** Suppose choices in (4)-(6) satisfy (7), and for
every cap in every selected deepest group they satisfy

    b_ij,1<=0,
    b_ij,2<0 whenever b_ij,1=0.                     (12)

Then for all sufficiently small positive t the actual projective image
family has maximum depth strictly below beta.

Proof. Every moved critical cap has Q_ij(t)<beta M(t), by its first
nonzero coefficient in (11). There are finitely many, so the assertion
holds simultaneously for small t. At each deepest base, (7) puts every
candidate point in at least one of these caps, giving it depth strictly
below beta. The finitely many old strictly cheaper whole-plane covers
at the other bases retain their strict gaps by continuity of the finite
fiber weights. The maximum of all these finitely many cap budgets is
strictly below beta M(t), so it bounds the depth of every candidate in
the full image mixed union. This proves a strict bound on the maximum,
not just individual nonuniform bounds below beta. All covering points
are in actual fibers, and all comparison caps are ambient closed
halfspaces. Their oblique normals have been retained in (5).

Consequently, at the stated projective local minimum there is NO such
finite two-jet satisfying (7) and (12). This is a rigorous necessary
condition even at all supporting-facet contacts and all other knots
of the polytope's cap profiles. It does not assert that this second-order
condition is sufficient for a minimum.

## 6. A finite linear feasibility test after fixing the first jet

Fix A,c_ij,s_ij satisfying the first-order parts of (7) and (12).
The remaining variables B,e_ij,r_ij enter (7)'s second-order part
linearly. In (10), E_ijp is affine in r_ijp when q_ijp!=0. When
q_ijp=0 it equals D_ijp(r_ijp), which is linear on each of the two
closed sign regions r_ijp>=0 and r_ijp<=0. Thus, after selecting one
of these signs for each of the finitely many zero q_ijp, all the
second-order conditions are finitely many weak linear inequalities
and strict linear inequalities in B,e_ij,r_ij, with known constant
terms. The choices of signs form a finite list, and their union is
the exact second-order feasibility test for this fixed first jet.

In particular a supporting-facet branch cannot be silently chosen in
advance independently of the actual threshold acceleration. Both
branches are examined, with their corresponding sign constraints.
The constants of these linear problems come from the actual cap
volumes and one-sided profile derivatives. No numerical solution or
approximate infeasibility is claimed as a proof here.

## 7. Scope in the current proof search

A strict bad finite positive family can be approximated by an actual
polytopal family with each fiber retained in Hausdorff distance and
depth convergence, as proved in the earlier compactness source. For
one fixed such family, projective transformations preserve polytopes.
Thus the attained projective-orbit minimum, when justified by the
separate smaller-base induction and orbit-attainment theorem, is
polytopal. There is no need to assume a C2 profile at that minimum
to use the present descent test.

This observation does NOT make a shape minimum polytopal, or identify
the two different extrema. Nor does it prove the existence of a
descent jet whenever beta<gamma_d/h(P). That is a new required
inequality/feasibility statement; it is not assumed in this note.
The general numerical OC implication remains unproved.
